newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain will ask EU to adopt its Cuba policy.
newsitem.headline: Spain will ask EU to adopt its Cuba policy.

text.p: Spain will ask the European Union to adopt its Cuba policy as a unified stance urging democractic reforms and respect for human rights, a Foreign Ministry official said on Wednesday.
Spain is to present its proposal at an EU committee meeting on Latin America in Brussels on Thursday.
"The Spanish delegation is going to propose the European Union adopt the policy of the Spanish government since May, the same line," said the official, who asked not to be named.
"This policy is based on the promotion of democracy and respect for human rights," the official added.
Spain and Cuba have had close ties historically. But the new conservative government of Prime Minister Jose Maria Aznar, which came to power in May, has taken a tougher line than its predecessor.
Foreign Minister Abel Matutes said last week that cooperation and aid to Cuba should be linked to political and economic liberalisation.
Spain will urge the EU as well to link increases in aid to reforms, the official said.
"The Spanish proposal also underscores the importance of EU member states coordinating positions in respect to Cuba in international organisations," the official said.
Spain will cite the unified European Union vote on Tuesday in the U.N. General Assembly against the U.S. economic embargo of Cuba as an example of the kind of coordination it is seeking.
The European Union has already united in one position on Cuba -- fierce opposition to the U.S. Helms Burton law.
The law gives Cuban-Americans the right to sue foreign companies that own or operate properties seized by the Cuban government from exiles after the 1959 communist revolution.
